newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung up on U.S. book-bill ratio news.
newsitem.headline: Samsung up on U.S. book-bill ratio news.

text.p: Shares in Samsung Electronics Co were strong in early morning trading on news that U.S. semiconductor book-to-bill ratios rose in October, brokers said on Tuesday.
The shares gained 2,500 won to 66,500 by 10:30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
The shares were also boosted by reports that Samsung Electronics had begun test production of its version of Digital Equipment Corp's Alpha microprocessor, they added.

"Samsung is in the spotlight this morning because investors feel the book-to-bill ratio and the Alpha chip tests point to an improvement in their business," said Lee Kye-joon, a broker at Daishin Securities.

The U.S. Semiconductor Industry said its book-to-bill ratio, which measures the value of orders against shipments, rose to 1.10 in October from 0.98 in September. The ratio means manufacturers received $110 in new orders last month for every $100 in shipments.
Limited samples of the Alpha 21164 chips were available, Samsung said on Monday.

This is the first product to result from an alliance between Digital and Samsung, which allows Samsung to become an alternate, second source manufacturer of current and future versions of Digital's high-performance Alpha microprocessors.
